articles.title: Argentina v Australia: men’s rugby union second Test – live
articles.summary: Updates as the Wallabies take on Los Pumas in Mendoza. Kick-off time at Estádio Malvinas is 6pm local/7am AEST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. It’s not a packed house unfortunately.
body: 27 min: Bell is held up over the line after Wilson cam agonisingly close. But there was another Puma slowing the ball down and it;s Molina who is yellow carded.

25 min: A bit of kick tennis has Gordon on the ball, gathering an attempted chip and chase from Roger. Gordon side-steps and looks up and sees that there’s a 50-22 on. But he overcooks it. No matter, they come back for an Australian scrum after a spill in contact by an Argentine carrier.

23 min: Efficient exit play. The Wallabies tried to run it out at first, but when Donaldson’s tip on didn’t find his winger inside his own 22, they saw reason and hoofed it clear. ~Argentina come back at them from halfway off a line-out. A pretty ordinary kick is comfortably fielded by Donaldson who returns a kick of his own with plenty of juice. Argentina pegged back in their own half.

articles.title: Seven points from three games - are Hull on track to avoid relegation?
articles.summary: It might be too early to settle survival talk, but newly promoted Hull City have given themselves the perfect platform to build on in the Premier League.
body: Sergej Jakirovic could not resist a joke when asked about Hull City 's remarkable start to life back in the Premier League on BBC Match of the Day.
"No, of course it is early," the head coach was quick to follow up.
Three games into a season is indeed too small a sample size to predict a club's fortunes.
But with seven points from a possible nine, three clean sheets and only two points behind early pacesetters Manchester City, the Hull supporters can be forgiven for dreaming a little.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
articles.summary: Celtic come from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren. Rangers beat Motherwell 1-0 but lose Shankland to injury. Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1.
body: Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.

The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal against Motherwell at Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.

Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.

articles.title: Audrey Werro fends off Femke Broeders-Bol’s charge in Diamond League final 800m
articles.summary: Swiss athlete wins by 0.06sec in meeting-record 1:54.75. Georgia Hunter Bell wilts to fourth in final lap of 1500m. In the last 30 metres of a boisterous and compelling women’s 800m Diamond League final, Femke Broeders-Bol slipped out of Audrey Werro’s slipstream and surged towards glory.
body: But as Broeders-Bol and Keely Hodgkinson have found repeatedly this season, the towering Werro is a mightily difficult athlete to knock off her perch. The Swiss athlete gritted her teeth, found a little more, and took the spoils once again.

“I felt her coming,” admitted Werro. “And I really enjoyed this battle because it pushes me to always work and not to really get in my comfort zone. I just keep in mind that one day I will get beaten. But now I just enjoy the first place.”

Broeders-Bol at least had the comfort of knowing that she had got closer than ever before – just 0.05sec behind Werro’s winning time of 1min 54.75. And when asked afterwards what made her Swiss opponent so good, she smiled.

“You should ask her because I would like to know,” she said. “But I think first of all she’s very strong in her mind. I think she’s a real fighter. She really goes for it with no fear and just all in. But I think just her last 200m is phenomenal. I think I could learn something from it but I think it’s her mind combined with her physical. She’s still so young, but so extremely fast.”

articles.title: From chess to battle for pole, Gasly has Russell covered at Monza
articles.summary: Pierre Gasly delivered the biggest surprise pole position in F1 for years in Italy as the leading contenders had scrappy qualifying sessions.
body: A quarter of an hour before the qualifying session which delivered the biggest surprise pole position in Formula 1 for years, Alpine's Pierre Gasly was playing online chess with Mercedes driver George Russell and winning.
"I must say before the quali, I felt pretty confident," the Frenchman said, "because I was picking piece by piece after piece."
Gasly said he reacted with a swear word but he was smiling as he recalled the moment.
"Turned out that it worked out well. So yeah, it's been fun," he added.

articles.title: Roma credit belief and insist want to ‘do even better this season’
articles.summary: Matias Soulé and Mario Hermoso said Roma ‘believed to the end’ in their turnaround victory over Atalanta and won’t shy away from Scudetto talk. ‘We want to do even better.’ It was another dramatic turnaround in Serie A today, as the Giallorossi had been trailing to the Ederson goal that came very…
body: Santiago Castro was frustrated at hitting the woodwork twice, and Marco Carnesecchi made several big saves, but they finally made all the pressure count in added time with the Hermoso looping header on a corner and Soulé drilling into the near bottom corner.

“I think we played well, we had the chances to score earlier, but the team believed to the end, that is what we want to do. We want to win, it was a home match and our fans gave us strength, so we are happy,” Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia.
“My goal was the equaliser, and it gave us all the realisation we could go on and win it.”
The statistics make it clear that Roma deserved the victory, as they had 66.5 per cent possession, 10 shots on target to two, and 39 overall attempts on goal to six.

articles.title: Gauff progresses at US Open, compatriots Fritz, Anisimova, Keys knocked out
articles.summary: Coco Gauff ensured the watching American public had something to cheer at the US Open as she progressed to the fourth round on a day when Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys suffered shock defeats.
body: Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.
The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic vs the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot.
"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

articles.title: Kentucky Wins Will Stein’s Debut
articles.summary: Saturday marked the beginning of a new era for Kentucky football. Will Stein took over for Mark Stoops, who was fired after 13 years. The Wildcats went from having the SEC's elder statesman of coaches to the league's youngest head man.
body: Starting his first game since he was a senior in high school, Kenny Minchey looked every bit the QB1 the Big Blue Nation was hoping for. The junior led Kentucky to four first-half scores on the way to a 28-7 lead. Overall, Minchey completed 18 of 27 passes, including nine of his first ten for 301 yards and four touchdowns. In addition, his average yards per throw was a nice 11.1 on the day. He also spread the wealth around, hitting nine different receivers.

His two first-half strikes went to his tight ends. If you’ve followed Kentucky football for any amount of time, you know one thing the BBN has been asking for is more looks to the tight ends. His first touchdown was a 10-yard strike to Mikkel Skinner, who got his first career score on his first college catch.
The second score was a two-yard pass to potential all-conference player Willie Rodriguez. Look for that to be said a lot this year. Rodriguez had 48 yards on four catches.
Minchey wasn’t the only Cat having a great day. Let’s look at some more good performances as Kentucky wins Will Stein’s debut 45-13 over Youngstown State.

articles.title: Villa take first point but rue missed chances in Hull stalemate
articles.summary: Aston Villa picked up their first Premier League point of the season, but were left to rue missed chances in their 0-0 draw against Hull City.
body: After an improved performance against Arsenal, Unai Emery was hoping for better fortunes in what was his 200th game in charge of the Villans.

A positive start saw Nicolas Jackson head wide in the opening couple of minutes, before youngster George Hemmings managed the club's first shot on target of the season in the first quarter of an hour.

However, the reigning Europa League champions often lacked the imagination to concern the newly promoted Tigers, who looked the most threatening during the first 45 with their collection of long-range efforts.
That was until the start of the second half, which saw Villa spurn two glorious opportunities.
